steps.title: GrallocAllocator::allocate (AIDL, mapper4)
steps.description: AIDL IAllocator entry point. Decodes the opaque descriptor blob produced by IMapper::createDescriptor into a buffer_descriptor_t, then calls the shared HIDL-era allocate().

stops.note: Decode the descriptor bytes that IMapper::createDescriptor produced.
Hand the request to the shared allocator code.
Translate the result into an AIDL AllocationError.

steps.title: GrallocAllocator::allocate2 (AIDL V2, mapper5)
steps.description: Allocator V2 entry. Builds buffer_descriptor_t directly from BufferDescriptorInfo via toInternalDescriptor() (producer_usage == consumer_usage == usage).

stops.note: Copy BufferDescriptorInfo straight into buffer_descriptor_t.
Same shared allocator path as V1.

steps.title: arm::allocator::common::allocate
steps.description: For each requested buffer: allocate pixel memory, then allocate + initialise the shared-metadata dma-buf (name, default dataspace). Records the buffer for dump(). Returns handles via callback, then frees the allocator's own copies.

stops.note: Placeholder buffers get a 1-byte allocation later.
Compute the layout and allocate the pixel memory.
Metadata size = shared metadata + client reserved region.
Allocate the extra metadata dma-buf.
Write the buffer name into the metadata.
Store a default dataspace for the format and size.
Return the handles to the caller.
Close the allocator's own copies; the client keeps its dup'd fds.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_buffer_allocate
steps.description: Rewrites CPU_*_OFTEN to RARELY for BIG video usage, derives format/size for each descriptor, allocates dma-bufs, and assigns backing_store_id (pid<<32 | counter).

stops.note: Google video IP: CPU *_OFTEN becomes *_RARELY.
Pick the format and compute every plane's size.
Allocate the dma-bufs.
Give the buffer a unique id (pid << 32 | counter).

steps.title: mali_gralloc_derive_format_and_size
steps.description: Validates the descriptor, selects the allocation format (base + AFBC modifiers), validates it, then computes layout either via the Exynos path or the generic path.

stops.note: Reject bad usage bits and oversized requests.
Choose base format + AFBC modifiers.
Turn modifier bits into an allocation type.
Check the format supports linear or AFBC as chosen.
Exynos formats use their own size rules.
Everything else: generic stride/plane math.
Reported stride = plane 0 allocated width.
Add 256 bytes of EXT_SIZE padding.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_select_format
steps.description: Maps the requested HAL/flex format to a base format (get_base_format), then — unless Exynos/BLOB/usage==0 — derives producers/consumers from usage, intersects their capabilities, and picks the best compatible format with the most AFBC modifiers (get_best_format).

stops.note: Resolve flexible formats such as IMPLEMENTATION_DEFINED.
stops.text: const uint32_t req_base_format = get_base_format(req_format, usage, type, true);

stops.note: Exynos formats and BLOB keep the requested format.
Work out who writes the buffer.
…and who reads it.
Intersect the writers' capabilities.
Apply format-specific capability limits.
Grade compatible formats and pick one.

steps.title: get_best_format
steps.description: Finds compatible formats, grades each supported one by number of AFBC modifier bits; substitutes the best one only when neither producer nor consumer is the CPU.

stops.note: Step 1: collect compatible base formats.
Step 2: check every producer and consumer supports it.
Step 3: grade = 1 + number of AFBC modifier bits.
Step 4: substitute the best format only when no CPU is involved.

steps.title: get_alloc_type
steps.description: Turns AFBC modifier bits into an alloc_type_t: superblock type (16x16 / 32x8 / 64x4), tiled headers, multi-plane, padded, front-buffer-safe.

stops.note: AFBC defaults to 16×16 superblocks.
Tiled headers requested.
AFBC_PADDING usage pads the header stride.

steps.title: prepare_descriptor_exynos_formats
steps.description: Exynos/SBWC formats: per-format width/height pre-alignment then setup_* helper fills plane sizes/strides/fd indices; GPU usage forces 64-byte stride (and rejects SBWC); each fd gets +1024 bytes, minimum 4 KiB.

stops.note: Per-format pre-alignment, then a setup_* helper.
SBWC with GPU usage is logged as invalid.
Add 1024 bytes per fd.
At least 4 KiB per fd.

steps.title: calc_allocation_size
steps.description: Generic path: per plane, align dimensions (get_pixel_w_h), compute byte stride (with HW/GPU/CPU/camera/BIG alignment via lcm), body size (+AFBC header), and plane offset.

stops.note: Round this plane's width and height.
Bytes per row for an uncompressed plane.
Combine hardware and CPU stride alignment.
Plane size = stride × rows.
The next plane starts where this one ends.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_ion_allocate
steps.description: Creates the private_handle_t and allocates one dma-buf per fd from the heap chosen by select_dmabuf_heap(usage). Optionally (GRALLOC_INIT_AFBC) maps AFBC buffers and writes initial headers.

stops.note: Create the buffer handle.
One dma-buf per fd.
Optionally write empty AFBC headers (GRALLOC_INIT_AFBC).

steps.title: select_dmabuf_heap / alloc_from_dmabuf_heap
steps.description: Picks a heap name from usage (exact-match list then subset list), allocates via libdmabufheap BufferAllocator::Alloc and names the dma-buf.

stops.note: Pick a heap from the usage bits.
Allocate from the dma-buf heap.
Name the dma-buf for debugging.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_ion_allocate_attr
steps.description: Allocates the extra shared-metadata dma-buf (cached system heap: SW_READ_OFTEN|SW_WRITE_OFTEN) into the fd slot after the buffer fds.

stops.note: Metadata lives in a cached system dma-buf.

steps.title: Mapper::importBuffer
steps.description: Clones the incoming native handle (dup's fds), registers it (validate magic + BufferManager::retain) and adds it to the registered-handle pool.

stops.note: Clone the handle: the fds are dup'd into this process.
Validate and take a reference.
Remember the handle so freeBuffer can find it.

steps.title: registerBuffer
steps.description: private_handle_t::validate (magic 0x3141592) then mali_gralloc_reference_retain.

stops.note: Check the handle's magic number.
Take a reference.

steps.title: BufferManager::retain
steps.description: Creates (or finds) the per-handle MappedData record and increments ref_count. No mmap happens at import time.

stops.note: First import: create the record.
ref_count++ — nothing is mapped yet.

steps.title: Mapper::lock → lockBuffer
steps.description: Dups and waits on the acquire fence, validates the handle is imported, then calls mali_gralloc_lock with the access rectangle.

stops.note: Take ownership of the acquire fence.
Wait until the producer has finished writing.
Map and lock for the CPU.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_lock
steps.description: Validates region/usage (rejects AFBC buffers), lazily maps the buffer, returns the base address, sets cpu_read/cpu_write and (if GRALLOC_ION_SYNC_ON_LOCK) starts dma-buf CPU sync; increments locked_ref_count.

stops.note: Check region, usage and compression.
stops.text: status = validate_lock_input_parameters(buffer, l, t, w, h, usage);

stops.note: mmap on first lock.
Hand back the CPU pointer.
Start CPU access (cache sync if enabled).
locked_ref_count++.

steps.title: validate_lock_input_parameters
steps.description: Any modifier bit in alloc_format (i.e. AFBC) makes lock fail with GRALLOC1_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED; non-CPU usage fails with -EINVAL.

stops.note: Any AFBC modifier: lock is refused.
No CPU usage bit: lock is refused.

steps.title: BufferManager::map_buffer_locked → mali_gralloc_ion_map
steps.description: On first map: sanity-checks the dma-buf sizes (lseek) and mmaps every buffer fd; protected / NOZEROED buffers are not mapped unless PRIVATE_NONSECURE.

stops.note: Already mapped: nothing to do.
Check each dma-buf's real size.
mmap every fd.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_ion_map
steps.description: mmap(PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED) of each fd with its alloc_size.

stops.note: Secure buffers are never mapped for the CPU.
Map each fd read/write, shared.

steps.title: buffer_sync
steps.description: Records CPU read/write direction; with GRALLOC_ION_SYNC_ON_LOCK it brackets the access with BufferAllocator CpuSyncStart/End (DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC).

stops.note: Record whether the CPU reads and/or writes.
DMA_BUF sync start — only with GRALLOC_ION_SYNC_ON_LOCK.
On unlock: DMA_BUF sync end.

steps.title: Mapper::unlock → unlockBuffer
steps.description: Validates the handle and calls mali_gralloc_unlock; release fence is always -1 (synchronous).

stops.note: End CPU access.
No release fence: unlock is synchronous.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_unlock
steps.description: buffer_sync(TX_NONE) ends CPU sync (if enabled) and clears cpu_read/cpu_write; decrements locked_ref_count. The mapping stays until the last reference is released.

stops.note: End sync, clear the CPU flags.
locked_ref_count-- — the mapping stays.

steps.title: Mapper::freeBuffer
steps.description: Removes the handle from the registered pool, unregisters it, then closes the handle's fds and deletes it.

stops.note: Forget the handle.
Drop the reference.
Close this process's fds.

steps.title: unregisterBuffer
steps.description: Validates and calls mali_gralloc_reference_release.

stops.note: Release the reference.

steps.title: BufferManager::release
steps.description: Decrements ref_count; at zero, munmaps the buffer (mali_gralloc_ion_unmap) and metadata, and erases the record.

stops.note: ref_count--.
Last reference: unmap.
Delete the record.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_ion_unmap
steps.description: munmap each mapped fd region and clear cpu_read/cpu_write.

stops.note: munmap each region.

steps.title: mali_gralloc_buffer_free (allocator side)
steps.description: Called by the allocator service right after it hands the handles back (Allocator.cpp), closing its own fds; the client's imported clone keeps the dma-buf alive.

stops.note: Allocator side: close its copy of the fds.
